news_items.headline: MAR closed up 3.28% on May 27; investors assess breakout momentum
news_items.summary: Marriott International shares rose 3.28% on May 27, 2026, trading near 52-week highs amid strength in the luxury hotel segment.

news_items.headline: Susquehanna raises MAR price target to $385 citing strong luxury performance
news_items.summary: Susquehanna lifted its price target on MAR to $385 after noting strength in the luxury segment; flagged elevated valuation as a near-term caution.

news_items.headline: Argus raises MAR PT to $425 from $420, keeps Buy after Q1 earnings beat
news_items.summary: Argus analyst John Staszak raised the firm's price target to $425 from $420 and maintained a Buy rating following Marriott's Q1 2026 earnings beat.

news_items.headline: Wells Fargo raises MAR PT to $446 from $443, keeps Overweight
news_items.summary: Wells Fargo made a modest upward revision to its street-high price target on MAR, maintaining an Overweight rating.

news_items.headline: Truist Securities maintains Hold on MAR, raises PT to $356 from $350
news_items.summary: Truist Securities kept a Hold rating but nudged its price target higher by $6, indicating limited near-term upside conviction despite acknowledging improving fundamentals.

news_items.headline: MAR declares $0.73 cash dividend, ex-date May 22, 2026
news_items.summary: Marriott International declared a regular quarterly cash dividend of $0.73 per share with an ex-dividend date of May 22, 2026. Routine capital return.

news_items.headline: Marriott expanding portfolio with new development project and online hotel furnishings shop
news_items.summary: Marriott announced new portfolio expansion (development project plus an all-inclusive resort in Mexico) and launched an online retail venture for hotel furnishings, part of ancillary revenue expansion.

news_items.headline: Elevated valuations prompt cautious near-term growth outlook for MAR
news_items.summary: Some analysts note that MAR's current valuation is elevated relative to historical multiples, tempering near-term growth expectations even as fundamentals remain solid.

analyst_consensus.recent_changes: Multiple PT raises this week: Argus to $425 (Buy), Wells Fargo to $446 (Overweight, street-high), Susquehanna to $385, Truist to $356 (Hold). Consensus is split — some sources show Buy (avg of 26 analysts, ~$377 PT), others Hold (15 analysts, $285.87 PT); of 37 analysts, 9 Buy / 16 Hold / 1 Sell. Overweight-oriented firms skew high-conviction targets toward $425-$446.

earnings_context.notes: Q1 2026 earnings already reported and beat EPS expectations (~$2.60 EPS, +12.1% YoY), driving recent PT raises. Key 2026 earnings catalyst is a ~35% step-up in co-branded credit card royalty fees (Chase + Amex renegotiation), a one-time boost normalizing to high-single-digit growth thereafter. Full-year guidance: worldwide RevPAR +1.5% to +2.5%, net rooms +4.5% to +5.0%. Next earnings date not confirmed; Q2 2026 report likely late July or early August.
